scope: candidates at 1-based manifest positions 41-50 (0-based 40-49) of data/validation/self_run_p0_candidates.json, frozen order; 10 candidates, 26 arms; coordinator cross-check of primary abstracts, exact trial registry, and protocol classification
blinding: data/validation/self_run_p0_predictions.json, ~/.cache/sisyphus-p0-output and all model outputs were NOT opened. FRDB snapshot (SHA256 647b80d9...9c7a verified) read for arm metadata only, with Cmax columns filtered out; arms were mapped by AUC / n / population comment. FRDB Cmax was not used for any mapping. Incidental exposure: frdb_11915 pk_funbound_comment (non-Cmax field) contains a median Cmax for the tolperisone whole group; seen, not used.
method_note: Single AI pass (no subagents), not an independent human verifier. Statuses: verified / verified_with_caveat / ineligible / unverified. IR not inferred from oral route. Paywalls time-boxed: Unpaywall + PMC + one browser attempt at the publisher (Springer, Wiley, Elsevier all paywalled/Cloudflare). Coordinator conservatively downgraded valspodar because the accessible abstract does not define subscript b; protocol-specific IR remains unconfirmed for milademetan.
unresolved_issues: Paywalled originals (need library retrieval): heptabarbital (Breimer 1975 EJCP), bitopertin (Boetsch 2016 Clin PK), methoxyphenamine (Roy 1987 J Pharm Sci), zopolrestat (Inskeep 1994 J Clin Pharmacol, 8 arms), tolperisone (Pawlowska 2015 EJCP, 7 arms).

Urapidil frdb_1254: Cmax 976.03 ng/mL read from open-access Table 4a, but '60 mg capsule' is very likely prolonged-release (Ebrantil retard-type; tmax ~3.9 h). Coordinator decides; recommend ineligible unless IR confirmed.
Valspodar frdb_6130: abstract Cmax,b/AUCb notation suggests blood and FRDB AUC matches, but b is undefined in the accessible abstract; source matrix remains unresolved. Do not score as plasma.
Cefteram (4 arms) and enoxolone (1 arm): analyte is the active moiety/metabolite of a different dosed compound (cefteram pivoxil; diammonium glycyrrhizinate) - candidate identities invalid for P0.
Tolperisone: 7 FRDB arms are overlapping populations (whole group plus genotype subgroups of 28 subjects). Prespecify an overlap-aware scoring rule before opening predictions; do not choose by error.
Heptabarbital: FRDB 200 mg arm cannot be mapped to free-acid tablet vs sodium-salt capsule without full text.
Methoxyphenamine: arm may be an acidified/alkalinised-urine phase (manipulated condition); only the uncontrolled phase would be eligible.
Milademetan: exact-study NCT03614455 registry confirms a 100 mg oral capsule, but IR behavior and salt-vs-base dose basis remain undocumented; source Cmax is a geometric mean.

candidates.name: VALSPODAR
candidates.source_identity: Kovarik JM, Purba HS, Pongowski M, Gerbeau C, Humbert H, Mueller EA. Pharmacokinetics of dexamethasone and valspodar, a P-glycoprotein (mdr1) modulator: implications for coadministration. Pharmacotherapy 1998;18(6):1230-6. doi:10.1002/j.1875-9114.1998.tb03142.x
candidates.candidate_notes: Wiley full text paywalled. Abstract reports valspodar exposure as Cmax,b / AUCb, and FRDB AUC 19.8 matches the abstract AUCb for valspodar alone. The accessible abstract does not explicitly define subscript b, however, so whole-blood matrix is strongly suspected but not source-confirmed; leave unresolved until full text is read.

arms.reason: Abstract's Cmax,b/AUCb notation and AUC match suggest a blood-based valspodar measurement, contradicting FRDB's PLASMA label, but the accessible original abstract does not define b or the specimen. Full text is needed to confirm matrix and formulation. Do not score this value as plasma Cmax.
arms.matrix: unresolved; abstract uses Cmax,b / AUCb, without defining b

candidates.name: HEPTABARBITAL
candidates.source_identity: Breimer DD, de Boer AG. Pharmacokinetics and relative bioavailability of heptabarbital and heptabarbital sodium after oral administration to man. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 1975;9(2-3):169-78. doi:10.1007/BF00614014
candidates.candidate_notes: Springer paywalled (browser: 'preview of subscription content'); Unpaywall closed. Abstract: plasma GC assay; crossover of 200 mg heptabarbital tablets vs hard gelatin capsules of an equivalent amount of heptabarbital sodium in 7 healthy volunteers. FRDB arm (200 mg, male, AUC0-12 14.6 mg*h/L, t1/2 7.7 h) cannot be assigned to the tablet or sodium-salt capsule arm without the full text.

arms.reason: Full text inaccessible. Plasma and single oral dose in healthy volunteers are stated in the abstract, but fasting state, table/Cmax, and which of two formulations (free-acid tablet vs sodium-salt capsule, which is 'equivalent amount' so salt-mass dose basis is unclear) this arm represents cannot be verified.
arms.formulation_evidence: abstract: free-acid tablets (Medomin) vs hard gelatin capsules of heptabarbital sodium; arm mapping unresolved

candidates.name: BITOPERTIN

candidates.candidate_notes: Springer paywalled (browser); Unpaywall closed; no PMC. Two fixed-sequence DDI studies in male volunteers; period 1 = single bitopertin dose alone. FRDB arm AUC is AUC0-312h (n=11), which matches the ketoconazole study's reported AUC metric, so the arm is likely ketoconazole-study period 1, but dose, fasting, formulation and Cmax are not readable.

arms.reason: Full text inaccessible. Abstract confirms plasma, healthy male volunteers, single bitopertin dose alone in period 1, but not dose (10 mg), fasting, formulation/IR, or Cmax value/table.
arms.matrix: plasma (abstract: AUC of plasma concentration-time curve)
arms.population: healthy male volunteers, n=12 per study

candidates.name: METHOXYPHENAMINE
candidates.source_identity: Roy SD, Hawes EM, Midha KK. Influence of urinary pH on the disposition of methoxyphenamine and three metabolites in humans. J Pharm Sci 1987;76(6):427-32. doi:10.1002/jps.2600760603
candidates.candidate_notes: Elsevier/jpharmsci.org paywalled (abstract only); Unpaywall closed. Five healthy EM volunteers, three occasions: uncontrolled, acidic (NH4Cl-type), and alkaline urine. Only the uncontrolled-pH phase would be a standard condition. FRDB arm (60.3 mg, AUC0-24 1315 ng*h/mL, t1/2 2 h) does not identify the phase; the short t1/2 hints at the acidified phase but this is not verifiable. 60.3 mg is likely a salt/base conversion (basis unknown).

arms.reason: Full text inaccessible. Plasma Cmax and healthy volunteers are stated in the abstract, but dose/salt basis (60.3 mg), fasting, formulation, the urine-pH phase this arm represents (acidic/alkaline phases are pharmacologically manipulated conditions) and the Cmax table are unreadable.
arms.population: 5 healthy volunteers, CYP2D6 EMs (MeSH Adult, Male, Middle Aged)

candidates.name: MILADEMETAN
candidates.source_identity: Hong Y, Ishizuka T, Watanabe A, et al. Model-based assessments of CYP3A-mediated drug-drug interaction risk of milademetan. Clin Transl Sci 2021;14(6):2220-2230. doi:10.1111/cts.13082 (PMC8604211); clinical study DS3032-A-U107 (NCT03614455)
candidates.candidate_notes: Full text read via PMC. Sequence AB Treatment A = milademetan 100 mg alone on day 1 under fasted conditions (n=18); sequence AC Treatment A was given 2 h after a full meal (fed, not eligible). FRDB arm AUC 14,698 ng*h/mL and n=18 match sequence AB Treatment A exactly; FRDB Cmax not used. NCT03614455 registry intervention independently specifies a 100 mg oral capsule for this exact study; its immediate-release behavior is not documented there.

arms.reason: Parent milademetan, plasma LC-MS/MS, single oral 100 mg under fasted conditions in healthy subjects (Results text: 'Following a single, oral, 100 mg dose in healthy subjects'). Arm mapped to Table 2 sequence AB Treatment A by identical AUCinf (14,698) and n=18. Caveats: value is a geometric mean (CV 26.4%); the exact-study registry confirms a 100 mg oral capsule, but immediate-release behavior and salt-vs-base dose basis are not stated; Cmax ratio is once called 'maximum serum concentration ratio' in the abbreviations but the assay and all methods are plasma.
arms.exact_locator: Table 2, Sequence AB, Treatment A (n=18); also Table 3 'Control Observed'
arms.population: healthy subjects; study total 36 (66.7% men, mean age 40.0 y)
arms.fasting_evidence: Methods: 'single dose of milademetan 100 mg on days 1 and 14 under fasted conditions' (sequence AB)
arms.formulation_evidence: NCT03614455 ClinicalTrials.gov record, Arms and Interventions: "Milademetan 100 mg capsule for oral administration"; release behavior unstated

candidates.candidate_notes: Open-access PDF read in full (journals.innovareacademics.in .../download/2902/pdf_350). FRDB arm AUCinf 6084.7484 matches Table 4a Test (fasting, n=9) exactly; FRDB Cmax not used.

arms.reason: Cmax read from source (Table 4a Test, fasting), but IR cannot be established: the paper only says 'urapidil 60 mg capsule' (test and reference products unnamed). Marketed 60 mg urapidil capsules (e.g., Ebrantil 60 mg retard) are prolonged-release, and mean tmax 3.9 h (test and reference) is consistent with a modified-release capsule. Recommend treating as ineligible unless an IR 60 mg capsule is confirmed. Other criteria met: plasma, parent, single oral dose, fasting, healthy adult males.
